title: rdoc (development version)
text: rdoc now offers three distinct type checking modes match different development stages: mode = "lenient" (default): Check typed code , ignore untyped functions. Perfect gradual adoption exploratory analysis. mode = "exported" (recommended packages): Require type annotations @export functions , internal functions remain optional. Inspired Rust’s #[warn(missing_docs)] public items. sweet spot R package development. mode = "strict" (maximum safety): Require type annotations functions warn using untyped function results. Similar Python’s mypy --disallow-untyped-defs. Migration: old strict parameter replaced mode. Update .lintr configuration: Example - Exported Mode:
code: # Old (no longer supported) linters: with_defaults(   type_consistency = rdoc::type_consistency_linter(strict = TRUE) )  # New linters: with_defaults(   type_consistency = rdoc::type_consistency_linter(mode = "strict") ) # .lintr configuration linters: with_defaults(   type_consistency = rdoc::type_consistency_linter(mode = "exported") )  # ✅ No lint - internal helper, no annotation required .helper <- function(x) x * 2  # ❌ Lint - exported function missing annotations #' Public API function #' @export add <- function(a, b) a + b # Error: Parameter 'a' missing type annotation (exported mode) # Error: Parameter 'b' missing type annotation (exported mode) # Error: Function 'add' missing return type annotation (exported mode)
